Initial conditions (on G_pol)
G_pol / G_ref, background or mean (g0)
Vmem branch where g is bistable

A homogeneous start in a symmetric tissue (rectangle, disc, ring, hexagon) keeps that symmetry exactly for roughly 5–10 simulated minutes, so patterns are mirror-symmetric about the N–S and E–W axes by construction. A random start, or a tiny σg (1e-6 breaks it within about 100–200 s), removes it.

Paint

Painting edits the current tissue, whatever initial condition it started from: run from a homogeneous or random start, pause, paint, and press Run to continue. It does not restart the simulation.

paint
value
brush radius (pixels)
clamp length (steps)

Vmem of painted pixels follows G_pol straight away on a fresh tissue and, on a tissue that has run, wherever g is monostable (below 0.80 or above 1.44); inside the bistable window a running cell keeps its Vmem branch, so the paint is visible in the G_pol view. Painted pixels get a yellow outline in every view until they are applied (Run or +1 s). Only tissue can be painted: pixels outside the shape (the checkerboard), including the part of the grid that a developing tissue has not reached yet, are ignored. Painting Vmem only has a lasting effect where g is bistable. “Initialise” restarts from the background and discards the paint.

colour range min

smoothing length (µm, Gaussian σ)

A Gaussian average over the tissue pixels, so the edge of the tissue does not darken, drawn with smooth interpolation. 5 µm removes the pixel-scale ripples, 7.5 µm (the default) also the cell-scale ones, 10 µm and more start to blur the structures of about 40 µm. The simulation, the colour range, the dashboard numbers, the saved state and the field range view keep the raw values.

“Sensed field / bias” is the perceived |E| divided by the threshold: above 1 a cell's G_pol falls (depolarising), below 1 it rises.
